Source check (grep):
- intro.tex:22 has the placeholder `% TODO(user): related work (Gromov 2023; Li et al. 2025; McCracken et al. 2025; Lyu & Li 2020)`. There is no related-work section.
- These bib entries are never cited in paper.tex or sections/: lyu2020gradient, gromov2023grokking, li2025nsum, power2022grokking. li2025nsum appears only in archive_v0.
- The mccracken2025 bib entry has the wrong title and author. The item's claim is accurate.

All pages below were fetched this session:
- Li et al. (arXiv 2402.09469v4, "AIStats 2025"), Thm 4.1: power neurons (u_1^T x_1+...+u_k^T x_k)^k w with ||theta||_{2,k+1} <= 1. gamma* = 2(k!)/((2k+2)^{(k+1)/2}(p-1)p^{(k-1)/2}). "For each frequency zeta in {1,...,(p-1)/2}, there exists one neuron using this frequency only", so the solution is dense. This is the b=nu endpoint, and they own the general-nu dense result.
- McCracken, Moisescu-Pareja, Letourneau, Precup, Love (arXiv 2505.18266). Cor 4.8: "Learning O(log n) distinct frequencies gives a logit margin Omega(log n)". The margin is unnormalised and the result is sufficiency only. One-hot one-hidden-layer MLPs learn floor(n/2) neuron types, and depth or embeddings cause a transition to "much fewer". They write "we don't know why it occurs".
- Jacobs-Montufar (arXiv 2605.19458, May 2026), Thm 4.9: max-margin reformulated as min sum |a_j|^{alpha/2}. alpha=1 gives sparse and alpha>=2 gives dense. No modular or Fourier content.
- Tian (arXiv 2410.01779, NeurIPS 2025 camera ready): semi-ring structure for quadratic 2-layer nets. "weight decay favors simpler solutions". No count law.
- Zhong et al. (arXiv 2306.17844, NeurIPS 2023): Clock vs Pizza algorithms, which depend on hyperparameters and initialisation.
- Doshi, He, Das, Gromov (arXiv 2406.03495; venue unconfirmed because Semantic Scholar returned 429): analytic many-term modular sum with phi(x)=x^S and cosine weights. Cross-terms vanish by random phase approximation as width grows. No norm or margin.
- Gromov (arXiv 2301.02679): analytic feature maps, found by GD and AdamW.
- Lyu-Li (arXiv 1906.05890, ICLR 2020): smoothed normalised margin increases under GD on logistic/CE loss, with convergence to KKT points of L2 max-margin.

WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200). Primary pages were fetched directly.

recommended_citations.why: Thm 4.1: dense max L_{2,k+1} margin for power neurons, with every frequency used. This is the b=nu endpoint that our universal bound recovers. Cite where the intro and approach discuss the b=nu recovery.

Cor 4.8: O(log n) frequencies give Omega(log n) unnormalised margin. Dense-to-sparse transition observed but unexplained. Replace the wrong bib entry, and cite at the intro count sentence and the log-scaling theorem.
Thm 4.9: a potential homogeneity exponent decides sparse vs dense max-margin neurons in general. Credit it for the generic idea; ours is the specific count for this task.
Algebraic (semi-ring) solution structure for quadratic nets on abelian groups; weight decay favors simpler solutions. Related work on solution structure, with no count law.
Trained modular-addition nets vary in algorithm (Clock/Pizza) with hyperparameters and initialisation. Background for 'trained networks do not look like this'.

Analytic solution for the many-term modular sum with x^S activation, where cross-terms cancel by random phases. Precedent for our n-operand (nu=n+1) constructions. Venue is unconfirmed, so it is cited as arXiv.
Analytic weights and feature maps for modular arithmetic, found by GD and AdamW. Precedent for the phase construction. Currently uncited.
GD on CE loss increases the normalised margin and converges to KKT points of L2 max-margin (not the global optimum). Justifies the max-margin endpoint. Currently uncited.

recommended_change:
1. Replace the TODO at intro.tex:22 with a related-work paragraph (move it to the appendix if space is short). Suggested text: "Max-margin feature theory. \citet{morwani2024feature} characterise the maximum $L_{2,3}$ margin of quadratic networks, and \citet{li2025nsum} extend this to $k$-th power neurons at $L_{2,k+1}$; in both, every frequency is used. Our bound recovers these at $b=\nu$. Why margins: gradient descent on cross-entropy converges to KKT points of the $L_2$ max-margin problem \citep{lyu2020gradient}, and weak regularisation approaches the global maximum \citep{wei2019regularization}; we make no claim that training finds the optimum. Constructions: analytic Fourier solutions go back to \citet{gromov2023grokking} and extend to many-term sums \citep{doshi2024polynomials}. Counts in trained networks: \citet{nanda2023progress,chughtai2023toy} report few frequencies or irreps, \citet{zhong2023clock} report algorithm diversity, and \citet{mccracken2025} show that $O(\log n)$ frequencies suffice for an $\Omega(\log n)$ logit margin while leaving the dense-to-sparse transition unexplained; our Theorem [scaling] supplies the matching upper bound and the norm-exponent explanation. That a homogeneity exponent separates sparse from dense max-margin solutions in general is shown for mirror flow by \citet{jacobs2026mirror}; \citet{tian2025composing} gives algebraic structure for quadratic-network solutions."
2. Fix the mccracken2025 bib entry: correct title, Gavin McCracken et al.
3. Add the bib entries jacobs2026mirror, tian2025composing, zhong2023clock and doshi2024polynomials.
